summary.en-US: Let AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other MCP agents) open tabs, read pages, click and type in your own Firefox, with your logins, while you watch. Needs the free tabdriver app.

description.en-US:
Tab Driver connects AI agents on your computer to your real Firefox. Ask your agent to open a site, wait for you to log in, and download last month's statement: it works in your own tabs, with your sessions, and you can watch every step.

**How it works**
The add-on talks to the tabdriver app on your computer (native messaging). Your agent runs the tabdriver MCP server, which sends it commands. Nothing listens on the network, and no data goes anywhere except to the agent you run.

**You stay in control**
- Agents can only act on tabs they opened or that you allowed.
- Controlled tabs show which agent is working, with a Stop button.
- Agents hand the tab to you for logins and 2FA, and wait until you click Done.
- Several agents can work at once, each in its own tabs.

**Setup**
Install the tabdriver app (macOS: brew, Windows: Scoop or PowerShell, Linux: install script), then add it to your agent. Instructions: https://github.com/trajche/tabdriver

version.approval_notes:
Tab Driver needs its companion app, which is open source (https://github.com/trajche/tabdriver) and published as GitHub release binaries.

To test:
1. Install the app: macOS/Linux `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trajche/tabdriver/main/install.sh | sh`, Windows PowerShell `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trajche/tabdriver/main/install.ps1 | iex`. This registers the native messaging host for Firefox (com.tabdriver.host, allowed_extensions tabdriver@firefox).
2. Install this add-on. Its toolbar popup turns green when it reaches the app.
3. Connect any MCP client, e.g. Claude Code: `claude mcp add tabdriver -- tabdriver mcp`, then ask it to "open example.org and read the page".
   Without an AI agent: clone the repo and run `make test-firefox` (Node + Firefox), which drives the add-on through the same MCP tools.

The add-on contains no remote or minified code. Page actions run in a content script (page-agent.js). One bundled function runs in the page's main world, only to dispatch file drops, because Firefox hides files that a content script adds to a drag event. The add-on never evaluates code received from the app.
